story:
Between the Bed, where Golestandt lies, and Moran's windy hill to the east there is a stretch of open moor that both sides claim. The stonelords who stand with the dragon say the moor is the Bed and every stone of it is hers. The elders and oracles on Moran's hill say the oldest stones were standing before she lay down, and will be standing after. The ground between is where the quarrel lives, and Agidad lives on it.

The hut-builders, the moor's first people, ran a row of standing stones across that ground, and Brother Aelred of Lostwithiel, who counted their hut circles for the Church after Arthur, believed it was a boundary: one side for the living, one side for whatever lay in the Bed. Agidad stands on the row. The drovers say he was one of its stones once, the tallest, and that when the giants of the moor stood up he stood up with them and did not leave his place. He goes from the Bed to the hill and back, and the giants on both sides let him, and the drovers call him the go-between.

What he carries between them, nobody knows. Some of the Prydwen clerks write that he is the Bed's envoy to the elders, and some that he is the elders' spy on the Bed. The oracles on Moran's hill, through the one drover who claims to have heard them speak, say only that a boundary does not belong to either side; it belongs to the boundary. The Stonecrush ogres say he is the giant they most want to eat, because a stone that both sides claim must taste of both.

He is not friendly. The drovers' saying is "give the go-between the whole road", and they keep it, and walk their cattle wide of the row. The pounders who work near him come when he is troubled, because the row is their work too, and the drovers who have seen it say a man who quarrels with Agidad quarrels with his masons as well. Only the riders come through untroubled, the drovers say, because a man in the saddle is going somewhere, and a boundary respects that.

When he is broken he stands up again before the dust has settled, and the oracles' word for it is the same as their word for a boundary stone set back in its socket: he is replaced, not raised. The moor needs somebody on the row.
legend: Agidad is a level 55 named granite giant in Dartmoor, on the open moor between Golestandt's Bed and Moran's hill. Despite what the old Dartmoor notes say, he is aggressive (the template the server uses sets aggro 200, range 500), and two granite giant pounders work about 360 from him and come in when he is hit, so pull him away or kill the pounders first. No spells or styles in the data: a melee fight with a 55 giant and his helpers, right for a group of fifties. Riding past on a horse is safe; walking past is not. Do not chase him east toward Moran's hill or west toward the Bed, where the stonelords are. He respawns in about 80 seconds.

loremasterTopic.text: The granite giant who walks the row of standing stones between [golestandt]'s Bed and [moran the mighty]'s hill, on the one stretch of moor both sides claim. The drovers call him the go-between and give him the whole road; his pounders come when he is troubled. The oracles say a boundary belongs to neither side, only to itself, and when he is broken he is set back in his socket, not raised.

bookPage: From the count of the hut circles of the moor, made for the Church by Brother Aelred of Lostwithiel. Between the warm ground and the windy hill the old people ran a row of stones, one hundred and four by my count when I came, and one hundred and three when I came back the next summer. The missing stone was the tallest. A drover showed it to me walking, half a mile off, with two smaller giants working at the ground behind it. He said its name was Agidad and that I should give it the whole road. I did. I have written the row down as one hundred and four, because the stone is still on it; it has only stood up.
